🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO MOVES TO OUTLAW "DRIP PRICING"</u>

Mexico's Congress is moving to kill "drip pricing" — the trick where an app flashes a cheap price, then piles on fees at checkout. A Morena reform to the Federal Consumer Protection Law would force delivery, ride-hailing and streaming platforms to show the "total and definitive price" from the first screen. Within days, the corporate lobby fired off letters to deputies demanding "working tables" to soften it — because transparency cuts into the margin.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Guanajuato Rides the AI Wave: $630M in Data Centers</u>

Guanajuato now hosts three data-center projects worth $630 million — two run by ODATA (Aligned Data Centers) in San Miguel de Allende and Apaseo el Grande — generating 200 direct jobs, plus a new $45-million, 60-MVA substation to power them. The state folded IT, AI and semiconductors into its "Guanajuato Suma" strategy, betting the reshuffle of global supply chains lands more high-tech capital in Mexico. (El Economista)

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Salinas Pliego's Reality-TV Land Grab Meets Garífuna Resistance</u>

Honduran police evicted a six-week "Camp for Life" so Mexican billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego's Grupo Salinas could film Survivor on the Garífuna beach of Uva de Cayos — blocking fishermen, cutting women off from water, and disrupting sea-turtle nesting. "A terrible repression is being fabricated. Once again they violate us," said Ofraneh coordinator Míriam Miranda — of the same tycoon fighting multi-billion-peso tax bills back home in Mexico.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Intelligence, Not Invasion: Mexico Captures a CJNG Regional Boss</u>

Federal and Michoacán forces captured Manuel Alejandro Rendón Aguilar, "Señor de la T," a CJNG regional coordinator linked to homicide, kidnapping, extortion and forced disappearance across five Michoacán municipalities. The security cabinet credited the arrest to "intelligence and investigation work" — coordinated surveillance between the SSPC, Sedena, Marina, the FGR and the state prosecutor.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Behind Mexico's Biggest Fuel-Theft Bust: The FGR Traces the Network</u>

The 59-million-liter huachicol seizure in Guanajuato — the largest of the sexenio — was only the opening move. The FGR, with Pemex Security and Logistics, is now tracing the fuel's origin, destination, and who built the clandestine infrastructure. Security chief Omar García Harfuch was blunt: "Of course there will be arrests — but they come later," as the investigation advances.

🇲🇽✊ <u>The 4T Doesn't Buy Votes — It Grants Rights</u>

In La Paz, Baja California Sur, President Sheinbaum drew the line against the neoliberal past: "Before, aid came only at election time to buy votes; now it's a right — direct, through the Banco del Bienestar, with no intermediaries." In BCS alone, 238,413 people receive welfare support — 4.465 billion pesos a year going straight to the people. "That's not buying votes. It's called building social justice."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Foreign Intervention Doesn't Solve Problems — It Causes Violence</u>

With Washington floating "intervention" against Mexican cartels, President Sheinbaum answered from Culiacán: "Interference doesn't solve problems — on the contrary, it causes violence." She confirmed every federal force — Army, National Guard, Navy — stays in Sinaloa "for as long as necessary," more than 20,000 already deployed, with her entire cabinet beginning weekly working visits to the state.

🇲🇽📊 <u>The Number Neoliberalism Said Was Impossible</u>

INEGI puts the urban basic basket at 4,905 pesos a month in August. Mexico's minimum wage — raised another 13% this year to 9,582 pesos a month, and more than doubled in real terms since 2018 — now covers that basket nearly twice over. Seven years ago the minimum wage couldn't buy a single basket; today it buys two.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>New York Looks South for Answers</u>

At the Urban 20 summit in New York, Mayor Zohran Mamdani singled out Mexico City's "Utopías" — the public centers for care, sport and culture built in the capital's poorest neighborhoods — calling the city "an inspiration" for a model that "places people and communities at the center of governmental action," as Head of Government Clara Brugada presented CDMX's fight against gentrification and displacement to mayors from 34 G20 cities.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Sheinbaum's Cabinet Faces Congress on the Second Report</u>

Sheinbaum's cabinet begins answering to Congress on September 29 over her Second Government Report: Finance, Education and Welfare in open session, while Interior, Security and Economy — Rosa Icela Rodríguez, Omar García Harfuch and Marcelo Ebrard — brief deputies behind closed doors. "Some issues, due to their confidentiality, cannot be disclosed to the public," said Morena's Ricardo Monreal, pointing to live anti-cartel operations and the T-MEC talks with Washington.
